issue.title: test: eight Codex keychain tests fail on Windows (secret_auth_storage default) on main d783df46
issue.body:
On Windows 11 (amd64, go1.26.8, `CGO_ENABLED=0`), `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider -run 'TestCodexSignedInInKeychain|TestCodexKeychain|TestSavedButSignedOut'` fails 8 tests on `main` at d783df46, with and without any local change:

- TestCodexSignedInInKeychain (keyring, auto)
- TestCodexKeychainRefreshWritesItem
- TestCodexKeychainSwitch
- TestCodexKeychainAskedSeldom
- TestCodexKeychainPromptWaitedFor
- TestCodexKeychainRetry
- TestCodexKeychainSignOut
- TestSavedButSignedOut

The failure is the Windows default of Codex's credential store, not the fake keychain:

```text
codex_store_test.go:236: codexToken: "" Codex keeps its sign-in in Codex's encrypted auth storage (features.secret_auth_storage) (cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring" in %TEMP%\TestCodexKeychainRefreshWritesItem...\.codex\config.toml), which magpie doesn't read
```

The tests write a config.toml naming `cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring"` but no `[features] secret_auth_storage`, so on Windows the reader takes keyring as encrypted storage (its Windows default) and refuses, while the tests expect the macOS keychain path the fake `codexKeychain` stands in for.

This is not a Windows-CI red (CI only compiles tests there); it shows when the package is run on the Windows box. Reported while verifying #2762 on this machine; no fix attempted here.

comments.body:
The cause is in the tests, not the reader: `secretAuthStorageDefault` in `internal/provider/codex_store.go` is on on Windows, and the tests write `cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring"` with no `[features] secret_auth_storage`, so there they read as Codex's encrypted store and never reach the fake keychain, while the setup already forces the macOS keychain path with `codexKeychainHere`.

The branch gives a test the macOS default for `secret_auth_storage` (off) in `isolate` and in `CodexKeychainForTest`, restoring it afterwards, so a config.toml that names no `[features]` is the item the fake keychain stands in for on every OS. `internal/agent`'s TestCodexSignInInKeychain had the same bug and is covered by the same hook.

[fix/2808-test-eight-codex-keychain-tests](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2808-test-eight-codex-keychain-tests), commit eed3fc9d9acd5ac9a5a7088ccfafd41577bd5a9b

Run: `TestCodexKeychainInTestsIgnoresCodexsDefault` failed before the change with the reporter's message ("Codex keeps its sign-in in Codex's encrypted auth storage (features.secret_auth_storage) ... which magpie doesn't read") and passes after; the eight reported tests, `go build ./...`, `go vet` for `internal/provider` and `internal/agent` (also with `GOOS=windows`), and `go test ./internal/provider -count=1` are green apart from `TestCodexAppServersOnHome`, which fails the same on clean `upstream/main` here (`HOME's .codex: not counted`) and is unrelated. Not run on a Windows machine itself.

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.

Still red on Windows (xiaomi-gpu, Go 1.26.8) at origin/main 67d0e4da6, each one alone as well. internal/provider `TestCodexSignInKnown` is red too, on the same Codex keychain group, and so is internal/agent `TestCodexSignInInKeychain`. The other Windows reds at that sha are in #4115, #4113 and #4114.

Taken properly this time — the re-test caught a real hole, and it is fixed; but the run at 67d0e4da6 was of main without the first fix, which lives only on the fork branch linked above and was never merged or cherry-picked there. So those ten reds are the unfixed set: the eight the issue names, `TestCodexSignInKnown`, and internal/agent's `TestCodexSignInInKeychain` — the last two read a keyring config the same way and were named in that comment as covered.

Still, simulating Windows here (below) showed the first fix did leave internal/agent's `TestCodexSignInInKeychain` red, for a reason the provider-side tests can't show:

**Root cause two.** `readCodexStoreSetting` folded Codex's OS default into what `filememo` keeps for config.toml, so the default was heard only until the file was first read. The agent test's setup (`codexHome`'s `provider.Save`, which looks for accounts through `Accounts` → `codexAccount`/`liveLogin`) reads config.toml **before** `CodexKeychainForTest` goes in, and that parse — made under the Windows default, where "keyring" with no `[features]` is the encrypted storage — stood while the file was unchanged, after the hook had put the suite on the macOS default. The item was never asked for. The provider tests never hit this: their `isolate` runs before any config.toml exists.

**The fix** ([fix/2808-keychain-windows-reds-v2](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2808-keychain-windows-reds-v2), on current main 1490045f5) is two things:

- the same two hooks as before: `isolate` and `CodexKeychainForTest` give a test the macOS default for `secret_auth_storage`, off, restoring it after;
- the default is no longer folded into the parse: `codexStoreSetting` keeps only what config.toml says (`Secrets *bool`, nil: not said there), and the default is read where the setting is asked of (`codexStoreSetting.secrets`). In production the default never moves, so nothing changes there; in a test it is heard even where the file was already parsed.

`TestCodexKeychainForTestIgnoresCodexsDefault` locks the second cause: a keyring config read under Codex's Windows default **before** the hook goes in must read as the item after. It is red under the first fix alone, green now; `TestCodexKeychainInTestsIgnoresCodexsDefault` covers `isolate`.

| Check | Command (this Linux box) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows simulated, plain main | `secretAuthStorageDefault` starts `true` — the one place GOOS feeds this decision; everything else reads the var — `go test ./internal/provider -run 'TestCodexSignedInInKeychain|TestCodexKeychain|TestSavedButSignedOut|TestCodexSignInKnown'`, and `./internal/agent -run TestCodexSignInInKeychain` | exactly the ten reported reds; `TestCodexKeychainFallback` and `TestCodexStoreNotReadIsLeftAlone` pass, as their absence from your list says |
| Windows simulated, first fix only | same | the nine provider tests green; internal/agent `TestCodexSignInInKeychain` still red — the hole above |
| Windows simulated, this branch | same, both packages whole | provider `ok`; agent `ok` except `TestDshACPSettingsGetTheRoute` |
| Native Linux, this branch | `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider` / `./internal/agent` | provider `ok`; agent `ok` except `TestDshACPSettingsGetTheRoute`, which fails the same on clean main here (a umask assertion in `dsh_acp_test.go`, unrelated) |
| Gateway's Codex sign-in tests | `go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestSearchedConversationOnCodexSignIn|TestCodexSignInUnmaskedSwitch'` | `ok` |
| Format, vet, build | `gofmt -l` on the changed files; `go vet`, `go build` for linux, and darwin/windows with `-tags nogui` | clean (`skillgit_test.go` is unformatted on main already) |

**Not verified**: a real Windows run. The simulation forces exactly the value Windows starts the var with, and the store decision consults nothing else OS-specific (backslash paths, file locking and Credential Manager play no part in it — `where()`'s GOOS check only words a message), but the post-fix green on hardware is yours to see with `win-run`.

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.

issue.title: 26 tests fail on Windows at main 6c1c0a74 (Windows CI only compiles them, so nothing shows it)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

`go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./...` on Windows 11 at `6c1c0a74` (= `origin/main`, fetched 2026-10-12) fails 26 tests in 8 packages. Windows CI runs `go test -run '^$' ./...` plus a short list of named tests, so none of these runs there. The workflow's comment says why ("Some tests fake a home through $HOME, which Windows doesn't read"). This issue lists what that leaves red, so later PRs can point to it instead of saying "the same on main".

Setup: Go 1.26.8 (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local`), Bun 1.4.2 on PATH, checkout with LF line endings (`git -c core.autocrlf=false worktree add --detach <dir> 6c1c0a74`). With the default `core.autocrlf=true` checkout, `TestPurposeAssetMatchesUsage` and `TestRedactKindsAreRedacts` (internal/gui) fail too; they pass on LF, so they are left out here.

## Failing tests, grouped by what the error points to

The groups are read from the error messages. **No cause below has been traced in code**; each is what the message suggests.

**A. The code reads Windows' APPDATA, the test moved only the home** (the folder found is under testenv's shared `AppData\Roaming`, not the test's own dir)
- internal/agent: `TestAlmaServerKeyed` (`alma_test.go:457`), `TestVSCodeInsiders` (`vscode_test.go:256: insiders dir …\magpie-test-home-…\AppData\Roaming\Code - Insiders\User outside …\TestVSCodeInsiders…`), `TestVSCodium` (`vscode_test.go:325`), `TestZedRelativeConfigDirUsesDefault` (`zed_test.go:405`).
- Probably the same: `TestSuffixModesReachAgentFiles` (`suffix_mode_test.go:78: on, codex: map[]`), and `TestCodexDaemonHelperIsNoStaleCopy`, `TestCodexStaleCopiesSayWhichIsLeft`, `TestCodexStaleOnlyForMagpiesChange` (`connect_stale_test.go`: 0 stale, want 1; `copies: []`).

**B. Unix file modes used to make a write fail** (a write the test expects to be refused succeeds on Windows)
- internal/agent: `TestAsideOfflineProviderWriteFailureRollsBackAllFiles` (`:530: provider write should fail`), `TestAsideOfflineWriteFailureRollsBack` (`:321: expected write refusal … <nil>`), `TestAsidePostReadFailuresNeverOfferOffline` (`:154`), `TestAsideDisconnectUnavailableOnlyAtInitialRead` (`:365`), `TestAsideOfflineLegacyRecordDoesNotResurrect` (`:298: record mode`), `TestAsideOfflineRestoresCompleteSelectionsAndPreservesUserChanges` (`:219: record mode`).

**C. A file still held by a running process, or a rename refused**
- internal/gui: `TestGatewayFixQuitsOnlyAMagpie` (`gateway_takeover_test.go:131: take-over: {OK:false Reason:stuck …\magpie.exe}`), `TestGatewayHeldByAContainer` (`TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat …\magpie.exe: Access is denied.`).
- magpie (root): `TestPluginListSaysMiddleware` (`unlinkat …\magpie: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.`).
- internal/plugin: `TestLoadConcurrentWithSavesAndEdits` (`store_test.go:281: rename …\.plugins.json.N …\plugins.json: Access is denied.`).

**D. A fake executable that isn't a Windows program**
- internal/gui: `TestUpdateThatWontStart` (`update_blocked_test.go:71: relaunched 0 times`; the run logs `fork/exec …\magpie.new: %1 is not a valid Win32 application`).

**E. Each on its own**
- internal/gateway: `TestClaudeAsRootEnv` (`claude_subscription_root_test.go:128: want … "IS_SANDBOX=1"`). Root detection on Windows.
- internal/netproxy: `TestIPv4Fallback` (`v4fallback_test.go:65: dial tcp [::1]:…: connectex: An attempt was made to access a socket in a way forbidden by its access permissions.`). Possibly a port in Windows' excluded range.
- magpie (root): `TestPluginOnOffRmShortName` (`plugin_middleware_cli_test.go:59: off by short name: err no plugin "zz-tags"`).
- internal/usage: `TestDesktopSessionAccountMetadata` (`session_provider_test.go:86: Code tab account mapping`).

**F. Intermittent on Windows** (re-run on HEAD, on an otherwise idle machine)
- internal/provider: `TestLoginUsageClaudeAskedMeanwhile`: 13 of 20 runs fail (`claude_usage_fallback_test.go:263: a reading from before the ask was kept`). This test does run on Linux and macOS CI (the "Race account usage" step), so if it fails only on Windows, that may point to clock granularity. Not checked.
- internal/gateway: `TestQueuedStreamKeptAliveOnceSentToItsVendor/responses`: 1 of 10 (`queue_keepalive_test.go:322: the agent wasn't kept alive before the vendor was asked`). Related to the queued-stream timing fixed in 3f4287e6.
- internal/agent: `TestWSLClaudeFollowerOnTheMainModelIsNoDrift`: failed in one full run (`claude_follow_drift_test.go:115`), passed in the next.

## Not known

- No cause has been confirmed in code; the groups above come only from the messages.
- Whether Windows Defender or the indexer holds files in group C: not checked.
- Linux and macOS results for groups A–E: not checked here. CI is green there, so these look Windows-only.

## Proposed

Each group is a fix of its own. A and B may mostly be test isolation, not product bugs: group A's code may be right to read APPDATA. Each fix should say which it was.

issue.title: provider: a Copilot token refresh holds every Copilot request behind one global lock

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
`copilotToken` (internal/provider/account.go, about line 1464) and `copilotDirect` (internal/provider/copilot_cli.go, about line 214) hold the global `copilotMu` while they fetch a new Copilot session token over HTTP (`http.DefaultClient`, no timeout of its own, only the asking request's context).

Every Copilot request on every account takes `copilotMu` to read its cached session. So while one account's token is being refreshed (within 2 minutes of expiry, about every 25-30 minutes), every Copilot request in the instance waits for that fetch to api.github.com. If the fetch is slow, all of them wait as long.

This breaks the code standard "nothing that can block runs under a lock its reader needs".

Found while looking at echo_ts's Discord report (#feedback, 2026-10-18): small Copilot requests are slower while a long session runs in the same magpie. This lock is not the cause of that report. It only stalls requests around a refresh, not all the time. But it is a real place where one request can hold up every other Copilot request.

Fix direction: fetch outside the lock, one fetch per GitHub token (singleflight keyed by token), with a timeout. Keep the cached session readable while the fetch runs.

issue.title: [Fix proposal] DSH-generated DeepSeek models need explicit thinking compatibility

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Tested patch: https://github.com/kupakupar/magpie/commit/24e86a625533512128d84c1bfee3a0ee59f86335

Compare: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...kupakupar:magpie:fix/dsh-deepseek-thinking-compat

A direct PR creation attempt through the connected GitHub integration returned HTTP 403, `Resource not accessible by integration`. Submitting the concrete tested patch here for upstream review instead.

When DSH is connected through magpie, pi-ai sees a custom provider named `magpie` at a loopback URL. Its provider/URL detection therefore misses DeepSeek's Chat Completions dialect: the selected reasoning effort is sent, but the explicit `thinking.type` toggle is missing.

This adds per-model defaults when magpie connects DSH or synchronizes its catalog:

```yaml
compat:
  thinkingFormat: deepseek
  requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages: true
```

They apply only to Chat Completions `deepseek-*` models offering an Off level, including nested relay IDs. Groups, unrelated models, models without a thinking toggle and other protocols keep their existing defaults. Explicit model settings and inherited route settings win, including `false`; the two model fields are no longer carried onto Responses/Messages after a protocol change.

DeepSeek already defaults thinking **on**. This fixes explicit on/off selection and assistant-history compatibility; it does not imply that earlier replies had no reasoning, nor change DSH's transcript folding.

The contract is documented in [agent-wiring.md](https://github.com/kupakupar/magpie/blob/24e86a625533512128d84c1bfee3a0ee59f86335/docs/subsystems/agent-wiring.md). Related to the narrower thinking-format part of #2889, rather than implementing general compat passthrough. Vendor reference: [DeepSeek thinking mode](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/).

### Validation

Code: `24e86a625533512128d84c1bfee3a0ee59f86335`, tested tree `f2aa7bba4da0d49e2ef0aa7c9e5565e3f194de19`, base `b641868e`. Go 1.26.8 on Windows amd64. Go checks used temporary HOME/USERPROFILE/XDG directories with GOPATH/GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE pinned before replacing HOME.

- Real fail-before/pass-after: the new generation/connect tests report missing DeepSeek compat without the fix; the protocol-change test reports leaked Chat fields; the route-default test reports a generated default shadowing the user's settings before that preservation fix.
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/agent -run '^TestDsh' -count=1 -timeout=10m`: **pass**.
- Actual generated config passed through the unmodified `@earendil-works/pi-ai@1.1.0` SDK extracted from DSH 0.2.1-rc.2: **17 cases pass**, using mocked fetch and synthetic history. Covers low/high/max, Off, reasoning/text SSE, reasoning/tool-call replay, the required field on a tool turn without reasoning, and an unrelated model. **Zero external vendor requests**.
- `gofmt -l`: empty; diff whitespace check: pass.
- `go vet -p=2 ./...` on Windows and `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui -p=2 ./...`: **pass**.
- Windows `go build` and Linux `go build -tags nogui`: **pass**; output kept outside the checkout and never installed.
- `go test -json -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m -p=4`: **exit 1**, not green. 11,013 passing test events, 557 skipped test events, 56 passed / 20 skipped / 8 failed packages. All **28 failing top-level tests** (32 fail events counting subtests) were reproduced with focused checks in a pristine worktree at the same `b641868e` base; details below. Existing reports include #1827, #2425 and #2808.

<details>
<summary>Existing failures reproduced on the unmodified base in this Windows environment</summary>

| Package | Tests and observed failure |
| --- | --- |
| agent | `TestAsideOfflineDisconnectRestoresWithoutDaemon`: missing-CLI fixture expectation; `TestCodexSignInInKeychain`: no detected sign-in; `TestCopilotFolderFromAnIDEPluginIsNotTheCLI` and `TestQoderSettingsFromAnIDEPluginIsNotTheCLI`: fake CLI not detected. |
| gateway | `TestClaudeAsRootEnv`: native Windows root detection; `TestSweepBridgeProjectsTakesOnlyTheBridgesFolders`: missing symlink privilege (#2425). |
| gui | `TestGatewayHeldByAContainer`: locked test executable during TempDir cleanup; `TestLodyImportHandoff`: AppData undefined; `TestPluginPageServedShutIn`, `TestPluginPageReadsWhatItDeclared`, `TestPluginPageNoAPI`, `TestPluginPageWebGuard`, `TestPluginPageActions`, `TestPluginPageWindowPolicy`: missing symlink privilege; `TestUpdateThatWontStart`: fake executable is not a Win32 program. |
| library | `TestRemoveFoundSkill`: missing symlink privilege; `TestGoneAgentListedToTakeOut`: Hermes skills fixture. |
| plugin | `TestWindowPageStaysInside`: missing symlink privilege. |
| provider | `TestCodexSignedInInKeychain`, `TestCodexKeychainRefreshWritesItem`, `TestCodexKeychainSwitch`, `TestCodexKeychainAskedSeldom`, `TestCodexKeychainPromptWaitedFor`, `TestCodexKeychainRetry`, `TestCodexKeychainSignOut`, `TestSavedButSignedOut`: Windows encrypted auth storage default (#2808). |
| sqlitedb | `TestSQLiteSurvivesMalformedEnv`: Windows rejects starting a subprocess with a malformed environment entry. |
| usage | `TestDesktopSessionAccountMetadata`: Code-tab account mapping (#1827). |

These are reported as failures, not treated as a passing full suite. They are outside this configuration fix.

</details>

No installed DSH desktop end-to-end test or native Linux/macOS runtime test was performed. No live gateway/configuration or installed official application was changed. No GUI assets change, so no browser UI suite was run. A textual merge check against `dd70c5e6` completed without conflicts; validation above is at the stated tested tree, not a runtime check of that merge.

issue.title: 22 more tests red on Windows at main 67d0e4da6, alone too (not in #1827/#1388/#2808/#1356)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Run on the Windows box (xiaomi-gpu, Windows 11, Go 1.26.8, `win-run`) at origin/main **67d0e4da6**, first in the package run (`go test -count=1 -timeout 45m <pkg>`), then each one again alone with `-run`. Every test below is red alone too, unless marked. None of these is in #1827, #1388, #2808 or #1356 (searched by test name); those issues' tests are still red and are commented there. The two package timeouts are #4113 (gateway) and #4114 (sessions).

The groups are read from the error messages. **No cause below has been traced in code** except where it says so. This box also has real WSL distros, so tests that look for WSL find them (Windows CI has none).

**A. A macOS or Linux case run on Windows paths** (the test doesn't force its OS, or builds a Unix path with `filepath`)

issue.title: internal/agent: six "kept" allocation tests red on Windows; each StampNow hashes os.Environ(), which allocates a string per variable there

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Not in #4115, #1827, #1388, #2808 or #4633 (searched by test name). Likely the same cause as #4633 (`TestResolveKeptAcrossRequests`) and #4115's `TestCodexListTagKeptWhileNothingChanged`.

Run on Windows 11 ARM64, Go 1.26.8, at v0.1.2519 (8ac1c7a5), alone with `-run` and in the package run. `StampNow`/`environSum` are unchanged on main 8f804396fd, and all six tests are still there.

| test | asserts | with the box's env (32 vars) | +38 dummy vars | 9 fewer system vars |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TestClaudeViaMagpieKept` | kept ≤ 20, kept×5 ≤ built | FAIL 67 / 461 | FAIL 106 / 539 | FAIL 59 / 445 |
| `TestMagpieModelsKeptWhileCatalogStays` | kept ≤ 200, kept×10 ≤ built | PASS | FAIL 106 / 871 | PASS |
| `TestViaMagpieKeptWhileCatalogStays` | kept ≤ 100, kept×5 ≤ built | PASS | FAIL 107 / 1910 | PASS |
| `TestWithViaKeepsTheJoinedList` | kept ≤ 60 | FAIL 67 | FAIL 106 | PASS |
| `TestOwnOptionsKept` | kept×5 ≤ built | FAIL 82 / 202 | FAIL 121 / 202 | FAIL 74 / 202 |
| `TestIsMagpieKeptWhileCatalogStays` | (cache hit) | PASS | FAIL | PASS |

(numbers are allocations a run, as the assertions print them; "+38" adds `TRIAGE_PAD_000`…`037`, nothing else changes. The `TestIsMagpieKeptWhileCatalogStays` row was run at v0.1.2310, a377ffde, with the same envs; the others at v0.1.2519.)

**Traced.** Adding 38 variables adds 39 allocations to every kept path (67→106, 82→121), and the built side of `TestOwnOptionsKept` doesn't move (202). Every kept path goes through `stampedLists.shared` (`route.go`), which calls `provider.StampNow` before it looks at its cache; `StampNow` calls `environSum` (`internal/provider/hold.go:80`), which ranges over `os.Environ()`. On Windows `syscall.Environ` reads the environment block and makes a new string per entry each call (`syscall/env_windows.go`, `UTF16ToString` in the loop, slice cap 50), so a cache hit costs about one allocation per variable. On Unix `os.Environ` copies a slice of strings already made, so it is cheap.

So on Windows the bars measure the size of the machine's environment more than magpie's cache. `TestClaudeViaMagpieKept` can't pass there at all: `syncHome` (`sync_test.go:25`) alone sets 23 variables, more than its bar of 20.

**Ways out** (not tried):
- make `environSum` cheap on Windows, e.g. hash the raw block from `GetEnvironmentStringsW` without making strings, or remember the last block's sum and compare bytes;
- or have these tests count allocations with `environSum` taken out (a test hook), and keep one test for `environSum`'s own cost.

`TestOwnOptionsKept` stays red even with the smallest environment tried (74 > 202/5), so it may have a cost of its own besides this one; not split out further.

timeline.body:
Taken properly this time — the re-test caught a real hole, and it is fixed; but the run at 67d0e4da6 was of main without the first fix, which lives only on the fork branch linked above and was never merged or cherry-picked there. So those ten reds are the unfixed set: the eight the issue names, `TestCodexSignInKnown`, and internal/agent's `TestCodexSignInInKeychain` — the last two read a keyring config the same way and were named in that comment as covered.

Still, simulating Windows here (below) showed the first fix did leave internal/agent's `TestCodexSignInInKeychain` red, for a reason the provider-side tests can't show:

**Root cause two.** `readCodexStoreSetting` folded Codex's OS default into what `filememo` keeps for config.toml, so the default was heard only until the file was first read. The agent test's setup (`codexHome`'s `provider.Save`, which looks for accounts through `Accounts` → `codexAccount`/`liveLogin`) reads config.toml **before** `CodexKeychainForTest` goes in, and that parse — made under the Windows default, where "keyring" with no `[features]` is the encrypted storage — stood while the file was unchanged, after the hook had put the suite on the macOS default. The item was never asked for. The provider tests never hit this: their `isolate` runs before any config.toml exists.

**The fix** ([fix/2808-keychain-windows-reds-v2](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2808-keychain-windows-reds-v2), on current main 1490045f5) is two things:

- the same two hooks as before: `isolate` and `CodexKeychainForTest` give a test the macOS default for `secret_auth_storage`, off, restoring it after;
- the default is no longer folded into the parse: `codexStoreSetting` keeps only what config.toml says (`Secrets *bool`, nil: not said there), and the default is read where the setting is asked of (`codexStoreSetting.secrets`). In production the default never moves, so nothing changes there; in a test it is heard even where the file was already parsed.

`TestCodexKeychainForTestIgnoresCodexsDefault` locks the second cause: a keyring config read under Codex's Windows default **before** the hook goes in must read as the item after. It is red under the first fix alone, green now; `TestCodexKeychainInTestsIgnoresCodexsDefault` covers `isolate`.

| Check | Command (this Linux box) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows simulated, plain main | `secretAuthStorageDefault` starts `true` — the one place GOOS feeds this decision; everything else reads the var — `go test ./internal/provider -run 'TestCodexSignedInInKeychain|TestCodexKeychain|TestSavedButSignedOut|TestCodexSignInKnown'`, and `./internal/agent -run TestCodexSignInInKeychain` | exactly the ten reported reds; `TestCodexKeychainFallback` and `TestCodexStoreNotReadIsLeftAlone` pass, as their absence from your list says |
| Windows simulated, first fix only | same | the nine provider tests green; internal/agent `TestCodexSignInInKeychain` still red — the hole above |
| Windows simulated, this branch | same, both packages whole | provider `ok`; agent `ok` except `TestDshACPSettingsGetTheRoute` |
| Native Linux, this branch | `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider` / `./internal/agent` | provider `ok`; agent `ok` except `TestDshACPSettingsGetTheRoute`, which fails the same on clean main here (a umask assertion in `dsh_acp_test.go`, unrelated) |
| Gateway's Codex sign-in tests | `go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestSearchedConversationOnCodexSignIn|TestCodexSignInUnmaskedSwitch'` | `ok` |
| Format, vet, build | `gofmt -l` on the changed files; `go vet`, `go build` for linux, and darwin/windows with `-tags nogui` | clean (`skillgit_test.go` is unformatted on main already) |

**Not verified**: a real Windows run. The simulation forces exactly the value Windows starts the var with, and the store decision consults nothing else OS-specific (backslash paths, file locking and Credential Manager play no part in it — `where()`'s GOOS check only words a message), but the post-fix green on hardware is yours to see with `win-run`.

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.
